statement: serve prints PROJECT02_GATEWAY=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/#token=<token> as its first stdout line once it can answer on that address.
notes: the harness reads this line to find the daemon

statement: While serving, <home>/daemon.json (mode 0600) holds protocolVersion 7, the token, the port and running {pid, startedAt}; a clean stop drops running and keeps token and port.
notes: format

statement: A later run on the same home answers on the same address (recorded port and token).
A daemon.json temp file left by a killed writer is removed by the next record write.
notes: pre-seed .daemon.json.<pid>.<uuid>.tmp; crash residue

statement: When another program holds the recorded port, serve binds a free port, prints "Port N was taken by another program; the address has changed. Open tabs and bookmarks need the new one." before the address line, and records the new port, which the next run keeps.
notes: the test's own listener holds the port a seeded record names

statement: SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP each stop the daemon cleanly: exit 0, empty stderr, and daemon.json no longer names a running process.

A stop with a turn in flight prints "Stopping; finishing what is in flight.", lets the turn finish (its POST answer, reply frames and turn_completed), then ends the streams, closes the socket and exits 0.
notes: stub provider holds the model call until after the signal

statement: After SIGKILL the record still names the dead run, and the next serve reclaims the home and answers on the same address.

A second serve on a running home prints "Already running on this home (pid N)." and the first daemon's address line, exits 0 with empty stderr and leaves the first untouched; once the first stops, a third run serves on the same address.
A serve started while the holder is stopping says on stderr that the holder is stopping and it is waiting, then takes the home over on the same address once the holder lets go.
notes: slow the holder's stop with a held turn

statement: A serve facing a holder that does not answer says so, waits for the lease, takes the home with the record's token and port if the lease is freed, exits 1 asking to run again when the wait (30 s) runs out, and exits 1 quietly without taking the home when stopped while waiting.
notes: SIGSTOP the holder to keep its lease silent, SIGKILL to free it; 30 s wait unless shortened

statement: An unreadable daemon.json (truncated, or missing the token) is replaced with a fresh token and stderr names the file.
notes: damaged record; a daemon.json that is a directory is refused instead (lifecycle.leftover-record)

statement: When the home refuses daemon.json, serve exits 1 with "Error: Local runtime store could not be written." on stderr and nothing on stdout, leaves no record and lets the home go, so the next run serves once it can write.
notes: chmod 0500 on the home: its lock directory still takes the lease

statement: serve refuses options it does not own (--help, --character) with exit 1 and "Unknown serve option" on stderr.

serve refuses to start, with exit 1, the reason on stderr and nothing written, when PROJECT02_TEST_DURATIONS names a key it does not read (the connector's edit among them), names one twice or gives one a value that is not a whole number of milliseconds above 0, or when PROJECT02_TEST_PROVIDER is set to anything but deterministic.
notes: hidden switches read once at start, absent from config.json and the settings page

statement: serve on a directory holding no store with stdin not a terminal exits 1 saying No Project02 store at "<dir>" and to re-run with --init, and writes nothing.

serve --init creates the store without asking and serves it, the home then holding exactly .locks, character-data, config.json, daemon.json and schema.json; a directory already holding only the store's own entries (characters, conversations, config.json) initializes too.
notes: format (layout)

statement: On a terminal serve asks No Project02 store at "<dir>". Create one there? [y/N]; yes creates the store and continues to the address; no, a terminal that goes away, or a stop while asking exits 1 and writes nothing.
notes: needs a pseudo-terminal in the harness: serve's stdin and stdout on one pty (python3's pty module relays it: the question shows, y creates the store and runs on to the address, the output CRLF with readline's cursor codes and stderr merged); the pipe-based serve() of harness/daemon.ts cannot, and a second spawn path would split the harness, so it wants a launcher option on serve()

statement: serve refuses to make a home of a directory holding foreign entries and creates nothing there.
notes: the refusal says only "Local runtime store is missing required files.", naming neither the directory nor its entries

statement: Initialization tolerates a live process's in-flight marker temp file but refuses a home holding an abandoned one from a dead process.
notes: owner check: refusing crash residue at init seems at odds with AGENTS.md section 2

statement: A leftover daemon.json counts as the home's own when the marker is gone; a daemon.json that is a symlink or a directory is refused.
serve --store naming a character data directory, or a directory inside one, is refused and nothing is created; a path that merely contains a character-data segment is a normal home.
A home whose lease is held by a live process on another host is never taken over.
notes: pre-seeded lock naming another host; format

statement: At boot every enabled character starts; a disabled one is not started: health shows it enabled false and not_started.

Until a model provider is chosen no character starts: health shows each failed with "No model provider is chosen. Choose one on the settings page." and an open is refused character_unavailable with that sentence.
notes: a fresh home chooses none

statement: GET /api/health lists each installed character with displayName, enabled and lifecycle state; a damaged character data directory does not hide the others.
Health carries protocolVersion, homeRoot, config diagnostics at their path and package diagnostics with the package path.
Starting an unknown character is refused unknown_character with a message saying it was not found.
A start sent while the same character is starting joins that start and answers only when the character is ready.
notes: not black-box as stated: a start is over before any request can meet it (a stream opened at once after the address line found all 13 characters of a home ready in its snapshot, 3 runs of 3), and nothing outside the daemon holds a start open

statement: A character whose config is invalid fails with a diagnostic naming the field; after the file is fixed an explicit start re-reads config and the character becomes ready.
A boot failure stays failed with its diagnostic until the stop: no retry publishes another starting state.
notes: the boot's own starting is over before a stream opened at the address line can see it, so the statement promises only what follows the failure

statement: A character whose boot failed on invalid config is retried by the next config change once the config is fixed, and becomes ready.
A character package that fails discovery is named on stderr with its code (invalid_descriptor) while the other characters are served.
A stop that races the boot wins: characters end stopped, later starts are refused gateway_stopped, the address line still prints, the process exits 0 and the record no longer names it.
notes: not black-box as stated: the boot is over before a signal sent at the address line lands (a stream opened at once finds every character ready), so a stop never races it from outside, and a later start meets the transport's 503 (transport.stopping-503), never gateway_stopped; a stop sent at the address line is lifecycle.stop-signals

statement: A stop issued during a character's reload wins (reloading, stopping, stopped).
notes: needs a stop inside a reload window; keep as a Rust unit test

statement: A stop during the automatic recovery after a fatal turn wins: no ready state is published after the stop began and the character ends stopped.
notes: not black-box as stated: the automatic recovery is over before a stop sent on the fatal turn's failed frame lands (the stream read failed, starting, ready, then stopping, stopped, 3 runs of 3), and nothing outside the daemon holds a recovery open

statement: A stop with a confirmation parked (and a reload queued behind it) returns promptly instead of waiting out the confirmation deadline; the character ends stopped.
Shutdown does not wait on a client that stalled mid-body.
notes: raw socket: headers with Expect: 100-continue, the daemon's 100 Continue, then half the body

statement: Shutdown gives a client that stopped reading a large answer the grace (about 2 s), then cuts it and exits.
notes: a turn's answer many times the socket buffers: a reply of control characters, six bytes each in JSON

statement: A first run on a home binds a free port of its own, names it in the address line and records it in daemon.json; two homes started together get different ports.
notes: stated in docs/wiki/gateway-api.html (Finding the daemon); no port is fixed in advance; whether the system or the daemon chose the port shows nowhere outside, so the row promises what shows

statement: A second stop signal during a stop ends the process at once; the lease left behind is reclaimed by the next start.
notes: stated in docs/wiki/gateway-api.html (Stopping)

statement: An /api request whose Host is not loopback is refused 421 misdirected_host.
An /api request without the bearer token or with a wrong one is 401 unauthorized; a malformed Authorization header is 400 invalid_request.
A request carrying a foreign Origin is 403 forbidden_origin; the daemon's own origin passes.
Every /api answer, refusals and the event stream included, carries Cache-Control: no-store.
notes: the wiki's rule is /api/*: the root's no-page 404 and a 404 outside /api carry none; the page's files are transport.page-files

statement: Every transport refusal is the envelope {"error":{"code","message"}}; a verb's domain outcome never uses it.

Every verb answers its domain outcome verbatim under 200 (health, open, start, a completed turn, a history page, an invalid page, pending confirmations, an unknown confirmation, a config view, an applied change).

A body that is not JSON, lacks the JSON content type, or has the wrong shape (missing fields, a stamp outside the pattern, a config query naming no target, a change without its value) is 400 invalid_request.
A request body over 64 KiB is 413 payload_too_large.
An unknown /api route, /api itself included, is 404 not_found in the envelope, behind the same auth (401 without a token).

The built page is served at / and under /assets without a token and with Cache-Control: no-store, HEAD answers empty, and a path climbing out of the page's root or naming nothing it holds meets the daemon's own 404 with no byte from outside.
notes: the asset is found through the page's own script tag, since a build names assets by hash; a page file named like an API path is not a state the shipped page has, so that clause is gone; pnpm check builds the page before the suites run

statement: Without a built page the root is a plain-text 404 naming /api.
notes: retired: the Rust daemon embeds its page, so a build without one is not a state a user reaches; today's page is looked for beside the daemon's own install, which one PROJECT02_SERVE_CMD cannot vary per test

statement: Once stopping, every new /api request is 503 unavailable ("The daemon is stopping.") while accepted work drains.
The daemon sends no CORS headers and accepts no cookie or query-string token.
notes: stated in docs/wiki/gateway-api.html (One way in)

statement: POST /api/conversations/open on a running character returns its direct conversation id, the same id on every later open, after a restart too.

POST /api/turns with a conversationId, a clientMessageId, a source stamp and one line blocks until the turn ends and answers completed with the committed user message and the reply under the character's display name.
notes: stub provider supplies the reply

statement: Open on an installed character that is not running is refused character_unavailable; on an unknown id it is refused unknown_character with a message naming the installed ones.
A delivery on a conversation the home does not hold is refused unknown_conversation.
A source stamp outside the pattern is a 400 invalid_request before any turn runs, and nothing of it reaches the stream.

A blank line ("Provide exactly one non-empty message.") or a line with a line break, Unicode line and paragraph separators included ("Provide exactly one non-empty single-line message."), is rejected input_validation_rejected with committed false: nothing is committed and the model is never asked.
notes: the end-to-end refusal is relayed by the connector (connectors.telegram-turn-ended-told)

statement: A delivered line is stored and shown trimmed of surrounding whitespace.
Committed messages get sequential ids <sessionId>:message-N independent of role.
notes: format (ids appear in history and anchors)

statement: One turn per (conversationId, clientMessageId): a repeat, while it runs or after it, gets the identical outcome and no second model request; a new id runs a new turn, and the same id on another conversation is another turn.
notes: stub provider counts calls; a repeat is observable only by its outcome and by the model's request count, not by whether it joined the running turn or read its outcome after; the statement promises what both show

statement: The same clientMessageId with other text is refused.

After a restart a clientMessageId whose line is already committed (also just before a rotation) is refused duplicate_submission, turn_completed says committed:true, and the line appears once in history.
notes: rotation via a small contextWindowTokens

statement: Without the conversation's record of taken lines, an open fails read_failed while the segment before the current one is unreadable, and open and history fail missing_file once its transcript is missing.
notes: rm of the record of taken lines, then chmod and rm on a segment; format

statement: One character runs one turn at a time, in arrival order: the model never sees two of its turns at once.
Two characters' turns run concurrently, each routed to its own character, and replies carry each character's display name.
A multi-line reply is committed and read back with its line breaks.

An interim visible_reply is committed and announced before the round's tools run; progress runs user_message, visible_reply, tool_calls_requested, tool_call_completed, then the next visible_reply, each message with its own commit record.
notes: stub provider scripts a tool round with an interim reply

statement: After a turn the model's output fails, the character stays ready and the next turn completes.
A delivery queued behind a fatal turn is refused character_unavailable rather than run after the restart.
notes: not black-box: a delivery shows outside the daemon only once it runs (the ready snapshot folds started turns), so whether it was queued before the fatal turn ended cannot be fixed from outside; CI run 39182409613 saw it arrive after the restart and run; the committed line, the one restart and the next turn are turns.fatal-turn-restart

statement: A turn whose reply the store cannot append fails on its answer with its line committed; the character restarts once (failed, starting, ready) and the next turn completes.
notes: split from turns.fatal-turn-refuses-queued: the clauses a client can see

statement: After a fatal turn the character recovers by itself; the next delivery on the same conversation runs without a reopen; a turn whose line could not be appended answers failed committed:false and turn_completed says so; an open sent right after succeeds with the same id, during the recovery or once it is done.
notes: chmod 000 on sessions/ and conversations/; whether an open lands during the recovery or after it cannot be fixed from outside; the statement promises what both show

statement: An unreadable conversations directory makes open answer failed read_failed (a storage outcome, not a 500), a conversation that cannot be written is failed write_failed, and open succeeds once the directory is readable.
notes: chmod

statement: After a restart a delivery on a conversation opened by the earlier run is routed from the stored record (character_unavailable until the character is ready, then completed on the same id) and history spans both runs.
An unreadable conversation record is refused conversation_unreadable naming the id.
notes: TS gap: a damaged conversation.json (not JSON) is refused conversation_unreadable with "Stored local runtime record is not valid JSON.", naming neither the id nor its file (a record its mode makes unreadable is refused naming its path, id included); pre-seed a damaged conversation.json

statement: History reads a conversation as one scrollback across segments: newest page first, chronological within a page, an earlier cursor walking back to the start, user lines with speakerName You, source and clientMessageId, character lines without source; without a limit a thread of 100 messages or fewer comes whole in one page.
notes: rotation via small contextWindowTokens

statement: History refuses an unknown or malformed conversation id unknown_conversation, and a limit outside 1..500 or a cursor it never issued invalid_page.
History reads a stopped character's thread; when the character's data directory is gone it fails missing_file.
Committed messages keep the speaker id and display name of the session's character; a reopened session continues under them; a speaker name edited on disk makes the open fail malformed_record.
notes: format

statement: A thread keeps the user and character names it began with: renaming the user in config or the character in its package never renames the thread, not even in its next segment; a thread begun after a rename takes the new name.
A history read without a limit returns at most 100 messages; limit accepts 1..500.
notes: stated in docs/wiki/gateway-api.html (Routes); the range half is pinned by turns.history-invalid-page

statement: Every stream without a usable Last-Event-ID opens with ready carrying protocolVersion, health, pending confirmations and pairings, and the running turns, as text/event-stream with no-store.
Frames are numbered <run16hex>-<seq>; ready carries the current number (-0 before any event); one data line of JSON per frame.
notes: format

statement: An idle stream carries a ": ping" comment every 15 s.
notes: 15 s unless PROJECT02_TEST_DURATIONS shortens it

statement: A turn's frames arrive in order: turn_progress user_message, reply_delta frames that join to the reply, visible_reply, turn_completed.
notes: stub provider streams the reply

statement: A stream returning with a Last-Event-ID the tail still holds gets resumed and then exactly the frames after it, byte for byte, then live frames under the same numbering; none when it holds the newest.
A Last-Event-ID evicted from the 1 MiB tail, past the newest, from another run, or malformed opens with ready instead.
notes: evicting needs more than 1 MiB of frames

statement: A stop ends each open stream only once every frame queued for it is written, a client lagging behind that keeps taking frames within the grace included; a stream asked for while stopping is refused 503 at once.
notes: pause a reader while frames larger than the socket buffers queue, signal, then resume it; a stream that slipped past the stopping guard, which ends at once, cannot be reached from outside

statement: A client that stops taking frames is dropped within the grace (2 s) and its stream closed.
notes: a reader that stops reading

statement: A stream opened mid-reply finds in ready the running turn (conversationId, source, clientMessageId) with its draft so far; a later ready carries a longer draft; after the turn ends ready carries no turns.
notes: the model server streams the reply at the test's pace

statement: A submission refused on the spot (sender_not_supported) completes at once without ending the running turn.
The person's line rides the stream as turn_progress user_message (speakerName You, text, source, clientMessageId) once durable, followed by the visible_reply.
A reply is drafted ahead of its commit (reply_delta under a draft id the commit then names); each reply of a round gets its own draft id (1.0, 1.1).
notes: stub provider streams visible_reply arguments

statement: Every draft a round opened is ended before the round moves on: a refused round's drafts and the drafts of a round the budget refuses are withdrawn (reply_withdrawn), and the next round drafts afresh (2.0).
notes: stub provider scripts the refused round; a draft an accepted round leaves uncommitted cannot be produced from outside (the NVIDIA adapter drafts exactly the visible_reply calls the decision commits), and one whose commit fails is stream.draft-never-a-message

statement: A reply whose write fails was only ever a draft: it is withdrawn, never announced as a message, and only the user line is in the log.
notes: needs the reply's write to fail after the user line landed; a Rust in-crate test with a storage double: no switch in the shipped binary fails a named write

statement: turn_completed carries characterId, conversationId, source, clientMessageId, status, committed and reason (a turn the model's output fails ends rejected, committed true, malformed_output).

A stream opened with ?connector=<id> counts the connector as present from before its first frame until its last stream ends (health_changed only when the count crosses zero); an unknown connector id is 400 naming the known ones.

A segment rotation that fails after a completed turn leaves the turn completed and the character ready, reports maintenance in health and as maintenance_failed on the stream, and an off/on cycle clears it.
notes: needs the next segment's lease held elsewhere; a Rust in-crate test with a storage double: no switch in the shipped binary fails a named write

statement: A tool call that needs approval parks a confirmation: it is listed by GET /api/confirmations with its deadline, stamped with the turn that raised it, and confirmation_requested reaches every client.
notes: stub provider calls runtime_plugin_config_update (demo-config tone)

statement: Approving answers answered, the turn completes, every client hears confirmation_settled approved before turn_completed, and the change lands; denying fails closed with config untouched and the model told it was denied.
A confirmation settles by its id alone; a second answer to the same id, or an answer to an id never given, is unknown.
A client that reconnects while a confirmation waits finds it in ready's confirmations, answers it over HTTP, and the blocked POST /api/turns then completes.
A confirmation nobody answers by its deadline (5 minutes) settles cancelled expired: the turn still completes, nothing is written, and a later answer is unknown.
notes: the daemon's own timer settles it at the deadline, so an answer at or past the deadline is answered expired only before that timer fires (the wall clock moved, as after a suspend), which no test outside can bring about; tests/unit/gateway-confirmation-broker.test.ts:85 holds that, a rust-unit row should

statement: An approval slower than the tool's execution timeout (5 s) but inside the approval window still applies.
notes: answer after about 6 s

statement: Stopping or switching off a character cancels every parked confirmation (confirmation_settled cancelled stopped); a confirmation raised while it shuts down settles cancelled without being announced; after a restart confirmations park again.
A connector's pairing request is pending under a six-digit code with pairing_requested on the stream, and asking again for the same subject returns the same request.
Approving writes the account into the home's pairedUsers, which every character inherits, with health_changed before pairing_settled and no character reload; asking again then answers paired.
notes: format (pairedUsers in config.json)

statement: A denial settles denied and writes nothing; a second answer is unknown; a subject of the wrong shape is 400.
Pairing is refused unknown_connector for a connector that does not pair, invalid_subject for a label with a line break, and an answer to a code never given is unknown.
A pairing request nobody answers within the hour settles expired on the stream and a later answer is unknown.
notes: the daemon's own timer settles it at expiresAt, so an answer at or past expiresAt is answered expired only before that timer fires (the wall clock moved, as after a suspend), which no test outside can bring about; tests/unit/gateway-pairing.test.ts:96 holds that, a rust-unit row should

statement: An approval that cannot be written answers failed with the reason, keeps the request waiting with what is left of its hour, and announces it again.
notes: chmod 0500 on the home: a read-only config.json alone does not stop the write, which replaces it through a temp file beside it

statement: A request whose account another settings window already paired settles approved without overwriting the name that window gave.
notes: save pairedUsers through POST /api/config while the request waits

statement: An approval whose write meets a concurrently moved config document is written again from a fresh read, merging with accounts already paired.
notes: needs a write landing between read and write; keep as a Rust unit test

statement: Pairing requests live as long as the daemon's run: the ready after a restart carries none and asking again makes a new one.
notes: stated in docs/wiki/gateway-api.html (A connector)

statement: GET /api/config for the home lists the host fields in page order with authored, effective and effectiveSource, every section the home may set, the documents' diagnostics and a fingerprint.

GET /api/config for a character shows values inherited from the home as effective but unauthored, the character's own overlay values, its own fingerprint, and package-required plugins as active even before she starts.

Views of an unknown or broken character are refused unknown_character (a broken one naming invalid_descriptor) and an unloadable home document is refused config_unloadable, never shown as blank fields.

A home without config.json views with no diagnostics: each host field that has a default shows it (contextWindowTokens 32768) and the rest, roleModelProvider among them, show no value (effective.source missing).
A declared default sits beneath every layer (effectiveSource default) and either the home's or the character's value overrides it.
POST /api/config applies set, unset, section_enabled and section field set/unset in one transaction and answers applied with the new fingerprint, which the next view carries.
A change presenting a stale fingerprint is refused conflict and writes nothing.
The fingerprint covers a secret's presence, never its value: two different values for one secret leave the same fingerprint, so two pages replacing a secret at once both succeed.
notes: security: the model can read the fingerprint

statement: A change is refused invalid for a wrong-type value, a value outside allowedValues, a non-authorable host path (storeRoot), an undeclared field or an unknown section, and unknown_character for an unknown target; a refused change creates no character-data directory.
notes: unsetting a required field is refused too, which no bundled plugin can show: retired with operator plugin packages

statement: A change to an unwritable home answers failed and leaves the fingerprint unchanged.
notes: chmod 0555 on the home

statement: Each target lists and accepts only what its scope may set: a write outside its scope is refused in both directions (a character-only section or field on the home, a home-only one on a character) and changes no file.
A change on a character target is written to character-data/<id>/config.json only, secrets included; the home's config.json stays untouched.
A value hand-authored outside its scope (a character-only plugin at the home, a field scoped the other way) warns runtime_config_authored_outside_scope at its path and never takes effect.

A character's overlay overrides the home field by field: host fields, a plugin's switch and settings (an overlay can enable what the home disables), and secrets (the home's fills in when the character has none).

A change reloads a running character only when what it runs would differ (its overlay or an effective value, a re-keyed provider secret), not for an overridden home value or a disabled plugin's settings; states go reloading then ready; a delivery sent as the reload starts runs first and one sent mid-reload waits and lands on the same thread.
notes: The clause on an upgraded plugin package went with operator plugin packages, which leave with the port.

statement: A reload that cannot assemble leaves the character failed with the diagnostic and no automatic retry; the next fixing change starts it again.
notes: hand-edit the overlay invalid, trigger with an unrelated change, then fix

statement: Switching a character off through a change publishes health_changed (enabled false) at once and then stops her; her view stays readable; switching her on starts her again.
A change that switches a character off while her boot is in flight ends with her stopped.
notes: not black-box as stated: a change POSTed right after the address line lands after the boot (a view and a health read sent at once on the address line found all 13 characters of a home ready, 3 runs of 3), and nothing outside the daemon holds a boot open

statement: A hand-edited unknown field is an error at its path: at the top level (or the retired project02.character) it blocks every plugin; under a plugin wrapper or a plugin's config it blocks that plugin.
notes: TS gap: at the top level (unknownField) and at project02.character the error is at its path in health and every character fails config_invalid, as stated; but one under a plugin wrapper (plugins.demo-config.bogus, runtime_config_unknown_plugin_wrapper_field) makes the whole home document unloadable, every view refused config_unloadable and every character failed config_invalid (src/runtime/config/mutate.ts:158 refuses a document on any load error), and one under a plugin's config (plugins.demo-config.config.nope, runtime_config_unknown_plugin_config_field) blocks that plugin alone only in the home's view: a character's view shows every enabled plugin but runtime.plugin blocked_by_config_errors and every character fails to start config_invalid, one with no plugin requirement too (src/app/activation.ts:625 blocks every enabled plugin once any error stands); health diagnostics

statement: A config section naming a plugin or connector this version lacks warns runtime_config_unknown_plugin or runtime_config_unknown_connector for that exact id, unless it is switched off.
notes: TS gap: a connectors stanza for a connector this version lacks warns runtime_config_unknown_connector at its path even when switched off ({"enabled":false}), in the home's view and a character's (src/runtime/config/connectors.ts:107, unknownConnectorDiagnostics never reads the switch); the plugin warning is skipped when switched off, but only a character's view carries runtime_config_unknown_plugin, never the home's

statement: An explicitly disabled plugin's incomplete or misspelled settings raise no diagnostics.
notes: TS gap: demo-config switched off ({"enabled":false}) with a misspelled field (nope) and a value outside its allowed ones (tone "shouty") raises runtime_config_unknown_plugin_config_field and runtime_config_value_type_invalid at their paths in the home's view and a character's, and every character fails to start config_invalid on it (src/app/startup.ts:391 and src/gateway/config.ts:208 validate switched-off sections); no bundled plugin has a required field, so incomplete settings cannot be shown

statement: An unreadable, malformed or wrong-version config.json or overlay is told apart (runtime_config_read_failed, runtime_config_malformed_json, runtime_config_version_unsupported) and an overlay's diagnostic names its character.
notes: TS gap: for config.json health carries runtime_config_read_failed, runtime_config_malformed_json and runtime_config_version_unsupported as stated, but no surface carries an overlay's code: health's config diagnostics hold the home's document alone (src/gateway/gateway.ts:640), her view is refused config_unloadable with the message, her health entry and start answer say "Character activation failed (config_invalid): <message>" (src/gateway/runtime/character-runtime.ts:1014), and inspect exits 1 with "Error: [character mira] <message>", the one message that names her

statement: config.json is a version project02.config.v2 document with a project02 section for host fields and plugins/connectors sections.
notes: format

statement: A malformed, unreadable (permissions) or invalid character overlay stops that character from starting with the diagnostic, writes nothing, and edits to it fail closed.
notes: chmod or a hand-broken overlay

statement: While the home's config.json is malformed, a character change is refused ('failed to load') and creates no overlay.
A config.json that is a symlink is refused by serve and by inspect, each exiting 1, and nothing is written.
notes: Today both say only "Error: Local runtime store is missing required files.", naming no file: a wording gap for a later fix, not a clause of this row.

statement: Secrets never appear in views, inspect or diagnostics, only as [redacted]; credential-looking field names (apiKey, token, nested access_token, dotted names) are redacted even when not declared secret.
notes: The undeclared-name half is shown with keys of telegram's pairedUsers: apiKey, token, a nested access_token and the dotted api.key.

statement: A secret is stored as typed and read by its plugin as written; a blank secret is refused when saved and is a runtime_config_secret_value_invalid diagnostic when hand-authored, as is a non-string one.
userDisplayName is trimmed, at most 128 characters and a single line; anything else is refused when saved and a diagnostic when hand-authored.
contextWindowTokens must be a positive whole number; 0, 1.5 or a string is refused.

nvidiaBaseUrl takes only an absolute http or https address without credentials, a query or a fragment: anything else is refused invalid when saved and is runtime_config_nvidia_base_url_invalid at its path when hand-authored, and neither repeats the value.
notes: security: a mistyped address can carry a credential

statement: A missing required plugin field is runtime_config_required_value_missing at its path (never naming a supplied secret's path), blocks the plugin unconstructed, and is required only of the scope that can supply it.

statement: Runtime management tools are offered and replayed under provider-safe names (runtime_plugin_list, runtime_plugin_config, runtime_plugin_config_update, character_state_patch) with their call ids kept.
Plain assistant content with finish_reason stop becomes the reply as written.
Native tool-call ids and arguments are kept for execution and replay; content beside tool calls is the model's note, never a second reply.
Streamed chunks are reassembled across arbitrary byte splits (content, tool calls by index, finish reason, usage); reasoning_content chunks and ping comments are ignored.
notes: stub provider splits frames and characters at odd byte boundaries

statement: Streamed plain content is never drafted (it becomes the whole reply at the commit); a visible_reply call's arguments are drafted as they stream with escapes decoded; content beside a visible_reply call is never drafted; text held back as a possible tag is released when the message is whole.

statement: A transient failure (503, 429, dropped connection) is retried and the turn succeeds; retries end after the last attempt with the final HTTP error reported; a 401 is not retried and fails the round provider_error.

finish_reason length, a missing finish_reason, a stream cut before its finish reason, a malformed chunk, or an error carried in the stream fails the round provider_error with no partial reply kept and the API key redacted.

Provider silence is bounded (30 s by default): the bound restarts when headers or chunks arrive, so a slow steady stream completes, while a chunk that never comes or a client ignoring the abort ends as a timeout.
notes: 30 s unless shortened

statement: Empty assistant content or tool arguments that are not a JSON object reach the decision parser as written and are refused and handed back there.
A prompt as large as the window admits (over 64 KiB of history) is sent and its exchange recorded.
A leaked think or reasoning block is scrubbed from the reply and kept nowhere, never drafted (whole or split); an unterminated block is refused by the parser, not a provider error.

statement: A round the runtime cannot use (no reply and no tool call, a blank visible_reply, non-object tool arguments, a blank reply beside a tool call) is refused whole with no tool dispatched, recorded, and handed back in exactly the next round as a system note quoting the error; the next round can recover.

statement: Closed JSON schemas are sent with strict mode; open unions and combinators are not marked strict.

statement: Prior turns replay natively: the user line, each finished tool round (the model's note and interim replies as assistant content with tool_calls, then each result as a tool message), then the final replies; unfinished calls are dropped and a rejected turn replays as its line alone; byte-identical after a reopen.
The model's note beside its tool calls is stored with the round's decision and never becomes a message.
Two rounds of one turn that said the same thing read back as separate replies; replies that normalize to the same text are both kept, normalized.

On rotation the summarizer is asked once (same model and server, stream false, max_tokens 3000, enable_thinking false, system = instructions, user = the transcript digest) and its trimmed text is carried into the new segment and replayed to the model.
Any summarizer failure (no key, HTTP error, blank text, length, network) is reported, never thrown, and a mechanical summary (turn count, dates, the latest things the user said) is used instead.

Wherever the daemon cuts text to a length (tool output bounded for the model, session-history snippets, the summary carried into a new segment) it cuts between characters: no half of a surrogate pair reaches the model or a stored record.
